A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same VLM4VLA study. All 23 pages, including equations, figures, tables and Appendix A.1-A.6, support reliable comparison; no material reading gaps were found.

before.justification: v1 reports original manipulation experiments on CALVIN, SimplerEnv and LIBERO, with benchmark results, auxiliary-task experiments and ablations in the main text and appendix.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and analyses, including benchmark scores and appendix ablations, with one revised baseline result.

M1.justification: The action-query token, MLP policy head, training objectives and action-token fine-tuning procedures remain identical, including the architecture details in Appendix A.2.6.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same CALVIN ABC-D, SimplerEnv-Bridge and LIBERO-Long evaluations, auxiliary training datasets and control-supervision task. No dataset, task or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain the same VLM backbones and expert baselines: OpenVLA, pi0 and, where included, ThinkAct. Appendix comparator sets are also unchanged; the revised pi0 score does not change comparator membership.

E3.justification: Section 3.3 and Appendices A.1-A.3 retain identical splits, image preprocessing, training budgets, model configurations, evaluation metrics and checkpoint/action-chunk selection procedures. No setting change accompanies the revised score.

E4.justification: The auxiliary-task, module-freezing, control-supervision and correlation analyses are unchanged. Appendix learning-rate, prompt-format, image-resolution and training-from-scratch analyses are also retained without revision.

E5.justification: Figure 4 retains the same across-checkpoint boxplots, and Appendix A.3 retains the same repeated-evaluation counts for pi0. No uncertainty-reporting practice, seed information or statistical estimation procedure changes.

E6.justification: Table 1 changes pi0* (PaliGemma-1)'s CALVIN Task-3 success rate from 0.786 to 0.686 under unchanged reported settings. Its other task rates and overall score of 3.509 remain unchanged, as do all other main-text and appendix results. This is a localized numerical revision, with no stated experimental rerun.

T1.justification: The action-mapping expression and training-loss equation are unchanged. Neither version adds or revises formal assumptions, mathematical derivations, theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims about VLM4VLA, limited transfer from general or auxiliary VLM capabilities, and the importance of adapting visual representations for control.

C2.justification: Interpretations of auxiliary-task transfer, the visual representation gap and control-specific supervision remain identical. The limitation concerning the absence of physical-robot experiments is also unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendices A.2-A.3 retain identical hardware, hyperparameters, prompt formats, architecture specifications and pi0 implementation details. Project-page and other resource-access information is unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2, the bibliography and comparisons with prior research are identical. No cited work or substantive novelty-positioning statement is added, removed or revised.

P1.justification: The first-page arXiv margin stamp changes from v1, dated 6 January 2026, to v2, dated 30 May 2026. Manuscript prose, title, authors and section organization are unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures, table structures, captions, appendix illustrations and manuscript layout are unchanged. The single Table 1 numerical revision does not alter its presentation; the margin stamp update introduces no document reorganization.

improvement.justification: The Table 1 correction resolves an internal inconsistency: pi0's five task-success rates now sum to the reported average of 3.509, whereas v1's entries sum to 3.609. It also restores nonincreasing success rates as sequence length increases. This is a limited improvement in reporting consistency; the methods, remaining evidence and conclusions are unchanged.
